findings.summary: Two catalogue sprites come out well under half their window, which makes the system worse than published here. At 1440px the backpack's ink is about 57px in a window about 201px wide (about 28%; about 32% at 390px), and the tote's is about 76px (about 38%). The other nine sprites are 41–45%. In the published version every grid sprite was 43–48% (1.2.0-rc.9 s2 home-desktop-dark.png) and detail sprites were 48–49%. 1.2.0 needed three rounds and a computed per-sprite check to reach that. This update replaced the explicit 40–50% band and its check with 'ink about half the window'. The agent then drew a tall item narrower than the 19-unit minimum and nothing caught it. The spec still has the 19–23-unit rule, but 'about half' with no lower bound or computed check lets it slip.
findings.promptFix: State the size of an item sprite as a range with a check: its visible ink spans 40–50% of the picture window's inner width at the narrowest and the widest grid width and on the detail page. An item that is taller than wide keeps 19–23 visible columns and gets taller; it never gets narrower. Verification: compute visible columns × unit ÷ window inner width for every item sprite from the code, and redraw any sprite outside 40–50%.

findings.summary: Several item sprites fail the name test at 1x. The skillet is a disc on a 1-unit handle, and the key ring is a large ring on a straight shaft. Both read as magnifying glasses. The tote is one arch over a box and reads close to a padlock, most visibly on the detail page. The tea towels are two plain upright slabs. Published samples had the same kind of misses (key ring and towels, skillet 1 of 3, tote 2 of 3), so this is not a regression.

The blog's ground strip is under its recipe. The cart sprite is about 10 units tall (the minimum is 14). The right-hand sprite shows only two floating light rails and a dash, because its legs are drawn in the outline tone, which disappears on the page ground. None reaches the 20–24-unit lead size. The other three apps' ground sprites (crates, kiosk, tree) are fine. The reference's footer trees and figure read clearly at the same size (p1-desktop-light.png).

On every settings route the sidebar panel stops about 50px above the ground strip, leaving a band of page ground under it. The spec's shell rule says the sidebar runs from the header to the ground strip, and the dashboard in this sample does that.

The apps disagree on two shell details. The store drops the container's side padding, so its content runs 72–1368px while the blog runs 96–1344px. The dashboard sidebar rows have neither the hue icon nor the bullet the Sidebar spec asks for, while settings uses bullets.

The blog's 'Subscribe to the newsletter' h2 has no dithered rule under it, unlike every other section h2 in the app and the published version's newsletter. The panel itself is the framed subtle panel the update asks for.

notes: SCOPE: screen step, 1 sample of each of blog, commerce, dashboard and settings (20261018-235602). No holdout apps were in this brief, so this run cannot show how the generalized wording carries to other products. Every gate passes (eval-1.md). Palette consistency is 0.938, type consistency 1, reference spacing overlap 0.892. The harness measured no layout defects, so there was nothing to confirm or dismiss. Known capture gaps, not penalized: the sticky header captured mid-page in full-page state shots (blog state-search-empty and state-newsletter-error, commerce state-checkout-errors and state-added-to-cart, dashboard state-empty-filter, settings state-profile-errors) and the dialog scrim ending at about 900px (settings state-plan-dialog). Light and dark captures are identical because the system is dark only.

PUBLISHED BASELINE: showcase/runs/night-cartridge/1.2.0/ holds only approval.json (carriedFrom 1.2.0-rc.9, evaluation 2), so the comparison uses the 1.2.0-rc.9 confirm runs (20261018-120446-s2 mainly).

UPDATE GOAL (generalization, 1.3.0): REACHED on everything this sample can show, except item-sprite size (the major). (2) Block meters: search and filter counts are now plain captions ('Showing 6 of 6 posts', 'Showing 11 products', 'Showing 8 of 8 projects'). Meters appear only against real maximums: uptime, the free-shipping threshold in the cart, '2 of 6 complete' tasks, '3 of 6 notifications on', and password strength. The published version's meterless deployments meter is gone. (3) Scenes per kind: blog articles share one article Banner (NEWS kiosk) and about has its own (READ hall). Product detail varies the sign word by category (BAGS, WEAR). The project detail, cart and each settings page have their own scenes. Nothing is repeated across kinds of screen. (4) Panels: the chart takes two shares beside the activity panel, and the bottoms are level with a stat row under a plot of about 200px. (5) Two-column layouts end within 160px of each other: product detail about 130px, cart 158px. (6) The footer form is a 2px-framed subtle panel opened by an h2 (see the minor about its rule). (7) KPI tiles go to one column at 390px. (8) Clamps: blog summaries are whole up to 4 lines and item summaries whole up to 3.

COMPARED WITH PUBLISHED: apart from the sprite-size major, nothing is worse. The hero lead keeps its defining features and a real sign (INK works: sawtooth roof, gear plate, chimney, stepped path; blog drawings/home-d1.png vs reference p1-i1.png). Garment sleeves stay attached and angle outward (commerce drawings/home-d7.png, home-d3.png). Banner leads are about 110px. The store name shows on mobile. Mobile tables pin Project and Status. Three issues are one-app slips against rules this update did not touch, so they are filed as minors, not as regressions of the prompt: the settings sidebar ending above the ground strip, the blog newsletter h2 without its rule, and the blog ground sprites. A confirm round would show whether any of them recurs.

SIGNATURE (4): present in all four apps and placed as Applying the concept says. That means the full-bleed hero, banners on articles, about and detail pages, strips on catalogue, cart, dashboard and settings, an inline figure in the article, framed vignettes in empty states (blog state-search-empty, dashboard state-empty-filter, commerce cart), the checkered ground strip on every route, the gold ▶ marker, and hue top bars with square bullets. Motion is stepped: nc-drift runs 120000ms with steps(48) on the blog hero (motion/motion-m1.png) and steps(20) on the product banner (commerce motion-products-canvas-field-tote-m1.png). The dithered halo moon is the spec's own recipe and matches the reference's haloed moon (p1-i1.png).

OTHER SCORES. Fidelity (4): night ground, cream pixel type, 4px windows, dithered rules under h2s, one gold commit with a hard shadow, hue bars, block meters and the grass strip, as in reference p1-desktop-light.png, without copying the cabin, figure or snow. Hierarchy (4): the scene and h1 come first, then 48px KPIs and prices and a gold primary action. Spacing (4): controls sharing a row share one height (email + Subscribe, Save + Reset, quantity stepper + Add to cart). States (4): card hover shows the marker and a lighter card. The first invalid field gets a gold focus frame and the rest danger frames with '!' messages. The plan dialog is a titled window with Cancel and a gold Confirm. Loading shows skeleton KPI tiles and a disabled 'Refreshing ...' button. Empty results show a vignette and a framed ▶ Clear filters. The user menu still opens with no option highlighted, as in published; that is a carried minor and not re-raised. Polish (4): radius 0, 2px and 4px frames, no browser defaults left over.

VERDICT INPUT: no blocker. One major, the item-sprite size. It is spec-caused (the 40–50% band and its check became 'about half') and there is only one sample, so it gates this screen. Five minors are listed once.
